title: Token-level observability: enhanced metrics, tracing spans, dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Anya Patel
description:
Motivation: We need better visibility into per-token cost and latency across the serving stack so product teams can attribute spend and latency regressions to models, prompts, and runtime configuration. Previous token-level metrics were limited to emitted token counts; this change pipes token timing, model variant attribution, and inferred token cost through our telemetry pipeline and ships dashboards + alert tuning to reduce noise.

This PR contains: 
- Instrumentation: add per-token timing spans in runtime span builder (start/end for generation tokens) and attach model_variant, route_id, and prompt_hash. Sampling is set to 1% by default; we expose feature flag to increase for canaries.
- Metrics: new aggregations in metrics exporter: token_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), token_cost_usd (sum/counter), tokens_per_request. Buckets rolled up by model, region, route, and billing_tier.
- Tracing: annotate spans with token_index and cache_hit flags; update span names to include model family.
- Dashboards: add Token Cost & Latency dashboard (panels for per-model cost breakdown, tokens-by-route heatmap, long-tail token latency table). Includes a pre-built widget to drill down to traces for offenders.
- Alerts: tuned alert rules to avoid alert fatigue: high token-cost-rate triggers only above 95th percentile of baseline for 12h and after sustained traffic; long-tail token latency alert now requires 100+ tokens in sample and a non-cache_hit ratio > 0.3.
- Backfill & Migration: exporters add a new metric namespace (redwood.tokens.*). Migration docs and console migration script included to update dashboard references.
- Tests: unit tests for metrics exporter, integration test simulating token streams, and a small e2e dashboard smoke test.
